rationale: The answer is a layer-4 dependency loop: 613.8a defines when one effect depends on another, 613.8b says a dependency loop is ignored and the effects are applied in timestamp order, 613.7/613.7a establish that the earlier-timestamped static ability (Blood Moon) applies first, and 305.7 states what setting a land's subtype to a basic type does (loses old land types and abilities, gains the basic mana ability).

Independence is decided by 613.8a, the resulting application order inside layer 4 is timestamp order (613.7, restated for layers 2-6 by 613.3), and 613.6 states that an effect applies to the same set of objects in every later applicable layer, which is why Life and Limb never picks Ore-Rich Stalactite up again.

605.1b makes Caged Sun's trigger a mana ability (triggers from mana being added, no target, could add mana), 605.4a states triggered mana abilities resolve immediately without players getting priority, and 104.4b states a loop of mandatory actions makes the game a draw.

608.2f states that an action taken on multiple objects is processed simultaneously, so every creature is destroyed at once while Timber Protector is still granting indestructible; 702.12b states an indestructible permanent can't be destroyed; 702.93a gives undying's return-with-a-+1/+1-counter behavior.

Kirtar's Wrath's threshold clause is a self-replacement effect (614.15), and 614.1 states replacement effects aren't locked in ahead of time but apply as the event happens, so the graveyard count that matters is the one at resolution.

121.5 states that moving cards from library to hand without the word 'draw' isn't drawing (so Abundance's cards weren't drawn), and 101.3 states an impossible part of an instruction is ignored, which is why Sylvan Library's 'choose two cards drawn this turn' and its life payment never happen.

611.2a states a continuous effect lasts as long as stated and, with no stated duration, until end of game, so Cytoshape's copy effect expires but the activated ability's type change doesn't; 205.1a states a card-type-setting effect replaces existing card types, leaving a noncreature enchantment.
508.1c is the step where attack restrictions are checked and 508.1k is the later step where chosen creatures actually become attacking creatures, which is exactly the ordering the answer relies on.
614.6 states a replaced event never happens, so Dryad Arbor never enters the battlefield; 116.2a/305.2/305.2b each state that a player may play only one land per turn.

614.6 covers the entering-the-battlefield event being replaced with exile; 116.2a and 305.1 state that playing a land is a special action the player takes (the land was still played, so Burgeoning's trigger condition was met).
The whole answer is the one-land-per-turn limit, which is stated independently by 116.2a, 305.2, and 305.2b (the latter counting lands already played regardless of where the card ended up).

701.6a states a countered ability doesn't resolve and none of its effects occur, so the creature card is never returned; 704.5m is the state-based action that would bin an Aura attached to an illegal object, and since Dance of the Dead legally enchants a creature card in a graveyard, nothing happens to it.

118.9 states that 'cast without paying its mana cost' is an alternative cost, 118.9d (and 601.2f) state that additional costs and cost increases still apply on top of an alternative cost, and 601.2g/118.2 give the player only a chance to activate mana abilities, so floating mana must be spent but lands need not be tapped.
508.1d states outright that if a creature can't attack unless a player pays a cost, that player is not required to pay that cost, even to satisfy an attack requirement.

113.7a states an activated ability exists on the stack independently of its source, so gaining control of the Equipment doesn't affect the pending equip ability; 109.5 states 'you' in an activated ability means the player who activated it (702.6a supplies the 'target creature you control' text), so it attaches to Autumn's Femeref Scouts.

614.12 states that replacement effects modifying how a permanent enters are determined from the permanent's characteristics as it would exist on the battlefield including other permanents' continuous effects, so Blood Sun's ability removal stops the ice counters; 603.8 states state triggers fire as soon as the game state matches, which happens once Dark Depths regains the ability.

709.3a states only the chosen half is evaluated for legality and put on the stack, and 709.3b states the other half's characteristics are treated as though they didn't exist; either states the answer.
205.4b states that changing an object's card types or subtypes doesn't change its supertypes, so an animated Gideon is still legendary while also being a creature.

608.2e/608.2f state that a spell's action involving multiple players and objects is processed simultaneously, so both permanents enter at once; 614.4 states replacement effects must exist before the event and can't go back in time, so Containment Priest can't affect a creature entering alongside it.

702.94a states miracle is a reveal-as-you-draw static ability linked to a triggered ability that lets you cast the card when it resolves; 603.3 states the triggered ability goes on the stack and stays there until it resolves, which is the window in which Vendilion Clique can be cast.

605.1a and 605.1b are the two criteria sets used to sort the list (activated vs. triggered, including the loyalty exclusion); 605.1/605.2 state that other effects and timing restrictions don't matter and that an ability stays a mana ability even when it can't produce mana; 605.5b excludes the sorcery.
117.4 states the top of the stack resolves only if all players pass in succession without taking actions in between, so Nikolas's mana ability restarts the sequence and Aiyana gets priority again.

601.2a is the first casting step (move the card to the stack), 601.2g is the later step where mana abilities are activated to pay, and 601.6/400.7 state that later illegality during cost payment doesn't matter and that the spell is a new object distinct from the exiled card.

701.6a states a countered ability doesn't resolve, so the sacrifice never happens; 603.8 states a state trigger triggers again once the previous instance has been countered or otherwise left the stack while the game state still matches.

603.3b states that a player puts the triggered abilities they control on the stack in any order they choose; 603.4 states an intervening-if condition is rechecked on resolution and the ability does nothing if it's no longer true, which is why no Zombie is created once Bridge from Below has left the graveyard.
702.61b states that triggered abilities trigger and go on the stack as normal while a split second spell is on the stack.

Leovold makes the draw an event that can't happen; 614.17/614.17c state that 'can't' effects follow replacement-like rules and that such an event can only be replaced by a self-replacement effect, and 614.7 states a replacement effect whose event never happens simply does nothing.
121.2 states cards are drawn one at a time, so Brainstorm is three separate draw events; 614.6 states a replaced event never happens, so Noe still hasn't drawn a card and Leovold never turns on.

The two principles the walkthrough runs on: 616.1 states the affected player chooses which of several applicable replacement effects to apply first (repeating until none are left), and 614.5 states each replacement effect gets only one opportunity to affect an event or the modified events replacing it.
614.5 states a replacement effect doesn't invoke itself repeatedly and gets one opportunity per event or modified event, which is exactly the 1 -> 2 -> 4 result with two Thought Reflections.
609.3 states that an effect attempting something impossible does as much as possible (101.3 states the same for impossible parts of an instruction), so Nico sacrifices the two permanents he has.

121.2 states cards are drawn one at a time, so the first draw happens before Leovold applies; 614.17/614.17c state that once an event can't happen only a self-replacement effect could replace it, so Chains never applies to the second and third draws.

603.3b is the APNAP process for putting simultaneous triggers on the stack (the nonactive player's Chalice trigger ends up on top and resolves first); 707.10 states that a copy of a spell isn't cast, so the storm copies don't trigger Chalice again.

305.7 (and 205.4b) state that setting a land's subtype doesn't add or remove supertypes; 305.8 (and 205.4c) state that a land without the basic supertype is nonbasic even with a basic land type, so only the one nonbasic land counts for Price of Progress.
603.7 states that an effect may create a delayed triggered ability that does something later, which is what Warrior's Oath's 'you lose the game' is and why it can be countered on the stack.

305.7 states what Magus of the Moon's subtype-setting does to nonbasic lands (loses old abilities, gains '{T}: Add {R}'), 613.6 states an effect keeps applying even if the ability generating it is removed (Humility stripping Magus's ability), and 613.1d/613.1f establish that the layer 4 type change is applied before layer 6 ability removal.

704.3 states all applicable state-based actions are performed simultaneously as a single event, 704.5g destroys the lethally damaged Lich's Mastery, 704.5a/104.3b make Nancy lose for having 0 or less life, and 104.1/104.2a state the game ends immediately when a player wins, so no further SBA check occurs.
800.4a states that when a player leaves the game all objects they own leave the game, which removes the Nefarious Lich Casey owns and sets off its leave-the-battlefield trigger for its controller.

601.2a/601.3 state that a player may begin casting by moving the card to the stack when nothing prohibits it at that moment; 601.2e is the later step where the game checks whether the proposed spell can legally be cast, which is what fails once Grid Monitor becomes the top graveyard card.
601.3 states a player can begin to cast a spell only if a rule or effect allows it and nothing prohibits it, which is the rule the answer cites directly.

601.2 lays out the casting steps in order (proposal 601.2a-d, then cost determination and payment 601.2f-h) and 601.2e is the legality check that sits before cost payment, which is exactly the answer's point that costs are paid after legality is checked.
601.3 states a player can begin to cast a spell only if a rule or effect allows it and no rule or effect prohibits it; Ixalan's Binding's prohibition applies and none of 601.3's exceptions do.

Two activations grant two separate instances of the triggered ability (113.10 covers effects adding abilities), and 603.2 states that any ability whose trigger event occurs automatically triggers, so both instances trigger and each gains 2 life.

The answer is pure layer order: text-changing effects (Volrath's Shapeshifter gaining the graveyard card's text) apply in layer 3 per 613.1c, before ability-removing effects (Yixlid Jailer) apply in layer 6 per 613.1f.
The answer rests entirely on a card fact (Golgari Brownscale has no dredge ability), not on any Comprehensive Rules text, so no inventory chunk states it.

603.10 states that some triggered abilities look back in time, using the game state immediately before the event, and 603.10a lists abilities that trigger when an object all players can see is put into a hand as one of those, so the graveyard state (abilities removed) is what's checked.

608.2c states a spell's instructions are followed in the order written, so the return happens before the sacrifice; 603.10/603.10a state the look-back-in-time rule that checks the object as it existed in the graveyard, where Yixlid Jailer had stripped its ability.
202.3a states that an object with no mana cost has a mana value of 0, which is how the revealed land wins the comparison when the other player reveals nothing.
702.29c states that 'when you cycle this card' abilities trigger from whatever zone the card winds up in after it's cycled, i.e. the graveyard, where Yixlid Jailer has removed the card's abilities.

614.12 states that replacement effects modifying how a permanent enters are determined by checking the permanent's characteristics as it would exist on the battlefield; its own example is a Yixlid Jailer / enters-tapped card put onto the battlefield from a graveyard.
